newsitem.title: USA: MedImmune, BioTransplant file IND on MEDI-507.
newsitem.headline: MedImmune, BioTransplant file IND on MEDI-507.

text.p: MedImmune Inc and BioTransplant Inc said Tuesday they have submitted an investigational new drug application to the Food and Drug Administration to begin the first human clinical trial with MEDI-507.
MEDI-507 is a humanized monoclonal antibody that the two companies said may have several potential applications in medical transplants and autoimmune diseases.
BTI-322, which has been evaluated in several transplant settings, is the rat form of MEDI-507, said Elliot Lebowitz, BioTransplant's president and chief executive officer.
Lebowitz disclosed the investigational application on Tuesday at a life sciences conference in London sponsored by the Union Bank of Switzerland.
Lebowitz said BTI-322 has provided encouraging results in initial clinical trials in the treatment and prevention of acute renal transplant rejection, Lebowitz said.

He said the two companies believe that MEDI-507 will retain its properties for those indications, with expanded potential for chronic administration as a treatment for autoimmune disorders such as psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatoid arthritis.

A Phase 1/2 clinical trial evaluating BTI-322 in the treatment of acute kidney rejection is going on at the Massachusetts General Hospital under an investigational application to the FDA by BioTransplant.
BTI-322, previously known as LO-CD2a, was discovered by Herve Bazin and Dominique Latinne, both doctors at the Catholic University of Louvain in Belgium.
